title: The picker names the option the conversation just named
description:
Reported from a live session, and reproducible from the code.

The conversation prints each option keyed by its id — `a) text-only — Hiç görüntü saklama…`, with its reason and what it costs later underneath. Then the elicitation prompt opens and shows three rows:

    ◯ Hiç görüntü saklama; sadece Türkçe metin günlük…
    ◯ Sadece hata anında, sadece arama bölgesi, kulla…
    ◯ Son N adımın küçültülmüş karesi yalnızca bellek…

No ids, and every row cut mid-word. The one token the reader was given to hold on to — `text-only`, `redacted-on-failure`, `ram-ring` — is the one token the prompt does not show, so the human scrolls back up and matches prefixes by eye, twice, to be sure. On a decision whose options open with similar words that check cannot be made at all.

Where it comes from: packages/mcp/src/ask.ts:104, `askChoice`, builds the requested schema as `enum: choices.map(c => c.id)` and `enumNames: choices.map(c => c.label)`. The host renders `enumNames` and truncates them; the id is the value sent back and never reaches the screen. The call site is packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts:339-348, which maps the options to `{ id, label }` with a comment saying labels only, on purpose — a host truncates rather than wraps, so long text is exactly what gets cut. That reasoning is right and is not what this node overturns. The bug is that truncation eats the handle instead of the prose.

The fix, and the whole of it: put the id in front, so what survives the cut is the part that identifies the row — `text-only — Hiç görüntü saklama…`. One expression, at the plan.ts call site or inside `askChoice` where every caller gets it. `askYes` and any other caller should be checked for the same shape.

The contributing half, worth one line while in there: `OptionInput.label` at plan.ts:37 has no length constraint, so a planning agent writes a sentence into the field the picker prints as a row. A short bound, or a describe() that says a label is a handle and not a description, keeps the rows readable even where the id is already visible.

The shape question this settles in passing, since it changes nothing outside these two files: prefix the id at the prompt, rather than teaching every host to wrap. SOBER does not control the host's renderer, and the M1 gate already established that it truncates; the only thing SOBER controls is what it puts in the first forty characters.

Acceptance: the elicitation rows begin with the option id, so a row cut short still says which option it is; the ids shown in the conversation and the ids shown in the prompt are the same tokens; a test asserts the leading token of each `enumNames` entry is that option's id.

brief.approach:
Score 3: one expression and one schema constraint, but the node's own text points at code that has since moved, so the first job is saying where the bug actually lives now.

**Where it moved, and where it still is.** The node names `askChoice` at `packages/mcp/src/ask.ts:104` and the decision picker at `packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts:339-348`. Neither is there today. ADR 0057 took the elicitation out of `decide`, `approve` and `accept` — the decision picker is now the host's own question tool, driven by the agent off `renderDecisions` text, and the ids are in that text. What is left of `ask.ts` is `askFields` (line 50) and `askYes` (line 104), and `askFields` builds exactly the schema the node describes:

```ts
enum: field.choices.map((choice) => choice.id),
enumNames: field.choices.map((choice) => choice.label),
```

Its one caller is `packages/mcp/src/tools/sync.ts:72` — resolving a merge conflict — and it is the worse case of the two the node was written about. `formFor` at `sync.ts:28-35` builds the choices as `{ id: 'ours', label: short(field.ours) }` and `{ id: 'theirs', label: short(field.theirs) }`: the labels are two truncated slices of the same record's text, which begin with the same words far more often than two decision options do. The host truncates the row, the reader sees two nearly identical cut-off strings, and the one token that says which side is which — `ours`, `theirs` — is the one token the prompt never shows. The archived form's `keep` / `restore` has the same shape.

**The fix, and the whole of it.** In `askFields`, put the id in front of the label:

```ts
enumNames: field.choices.map((choice) => `${choice.id} — ${choice.label}`),
```

Inside `askFields`, so every caller now and later gets it rather than each call site remembering. `enum` — the value sent back — does not change, so `resolveConflict` still receives `'ours'` / `'theirs'` and nothing downstream moves. Put one comment on the line saying why the id leads: the host truncates rather than wraps (the M1 gate established that, and it is why `sync.ts` passes `short(...)` in the first place), so whatever SOBER puts in the first forty characters is what survives, and the handle has to be in them. That is the shape question the node settles in passing — prefix at the prompt, do not try to teach four hosts to wrap.

`askYes` takes a `yes: string` for a single checkbox title, not a list of rows, so there is nothing to prefix there. Check it and leave it; say so in the commit rather than editing it.

**The contributing half.** `OptionInput` at `packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts:38` is `label: z.string()` with no constraint and no `.describe()`, while every other field in that object has one. A planning agent therefore writes a sentence into the field a picker prints as a row. Add a `.describe()` in the voice of its siblings — a label is a short handle a person reads in a list, not a description; the reasoning goes in `reason` and `costLater`. Prefer the `.describe()` over a hard `.max()`: a refused proposal for a label three characters too long costs more than a long label does, and the description is what the agent actually reads.

**Tests.** `packages/mcp/src/ask.test.ts` if it exists, otherwise beside the existing MCP unit tests — find them with `fd -e test.ts . packages/mcp/src`. One assertion is the node's: every `enumNames` entry begins with its own choice's id, so a row cut short still says which option it is, and the `enum` values are unchanged. If `askFields` cannot be tested without a live server, assert it through the conflict path in `test/integration/mcp.test.ts`, which already drives sync with a conflict and a fake elicitation client — extend that case rather than starting a file.

Nothing else changes: not `resolveConflict`, not `formFor`'s `short()`, not the decision tools, not the CLI.

acceptance.proves: the merge-conflict form still round-trips end to end: the rows now lead with `ours` and `theirs`, the values sent back are unchanged, and resolveConflict lands the same result

acceptance.run: git grep -q 'choice.id' -- packages/mcp/src/ask.ts && git grep -q 'enumNames' -- packages/mcp/src/ask.ts
acceptance.proves: the id is built into the rendered row inside askFields, so every caller inherits it rather than each call site remembering
it is the display list that carries the id — the `enum` of values sent back was left alone, which is what keeps 'ours'/'theirs' flowing into resolveConflict
OptionInput.label now tells the planning agent it is a handle and not a description — the contributing half, without a hard length refusal
only the MCP package and its own integration test changed: core, the schema, the CLI and the dashboard are untouched
the widened row strings and the described field compile
